title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a field of finite type over Q and K̄ is an algebraic closure. Grothendieck defines a 'D-structure' (D for discrete) on K̄. It consists of (a) the subfield Q̄ ⊂ K̄, and (b) for every algebraic curve X over K̄ of type (g,ν), a 'discretification' of the profinite group π̂_1(X). A discretification is a choice of a discrete subgroup isomorphic to the surface group π_{g,ν}, inside π̂_1(X) and up to conjugacy, of which π̂_1(X) is the profinite completion. The previous page says that such choices form a torsor under a subgroup M'_{g,ν} ⊂ Aut_ext(π̂_{g,ν}). The choices are presumably required to be compatible with morphisms and with the Teichmüller tower.

Special D-structures are those coming from an embedding φ: K̄ → C. For each X, take the image of π_1^top(X_φ(C)) in π̂_1(X_φ) ≅ π̂_1(X); this uses invariance of étale π_1 under extension of algebraically closed fields in characteristic 0.

Functoriality: any isomorphism ψ: K̄ → K̄' (in particular a K-isomorphism) transports D-structures and special D-structures. Hence Γ = Aut_K(K̄) acts on Discr(K̄) and on Discspec(K̄).

The 'Prop' asserts that two special discretifications Θ, Θ' on two algebraic closures of K are related by a K-isomorphism. The Corollary says Γ acts transitively on Discspec(K̄). The garbled parenthesis seems to qualify this: transitivity holds for the full group, not for a finite-index subgroup.

The NB records a commutative square. The top row is the transport map Isom(K̄,K̄') × Discr(K̄) → Discr(K̄'). The bottom row is Isom(K̄,K̄') × Hom(K̄,C) → Hom(K̄',C), (ψ,φ) ↦ φ∘ψ^{-1}. The vertical arrows are φ ↦ Θ_φ. So φ ↦ Θ_φ is equivariant, and for K̄ = K̄' this is the Γ-equivariance of Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄).

The purpose, continuing the previous page, is to recast the Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller groupoids as automorphisms of a 'discrete structure' on K̄. In other words, to compare Gal with the stabilizers of the discrete (topological) π_1's inside the profinite ones.

The next page pursues this:
- Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄) is surjective and Γ-equivariant.
- Transitivity is corrected to hold only when K̄ = Q̄.
- It asks whether the map could be injective, i.e. whether the topological fundamental groups of all curves determine the complex embedding.
- It suggests this forces K algebraic over Q.
- It turns to Hodge structures on π_1^ab ⊗ C as the transcendental invariant that would recover φ.
errors: As written, the Prop (existence of a K-isomorphism matching any two special discretifications) cannot hold in general. If K is a number field ≠ Q, Γ_K-orbits on Hom(Q̄,C) correspond to embeddings K → C, so a K-isomorphism cannot relate Θ_φ and Θ_φ' when φ|K and φ'|K are not related (complex conjugation fixes Θ_φ, so only those orbits merge). Hom(Q̄,C) is a torsor under the full Gal(Q̄/Q), not Γ_K. For K transcendental the transitivity claim is also unjustified. Grothendieck himself corrects this on the next page ('Γ est transitif * lorsque K̄ = Q̄'). The Cor's parenthesis about finite-index subgroups appears to be an attempt at this correction.

Implicit: Θ_φ is not injective in φ even for K = Q̄. φ and c∘φ (c = complex conjugation) give the same discretification, since conjugation is a homeomorphism X_φ(C) → X_{cφ}(C). So at best Hom(Q̄,C)/{1,c} → Discspec could be injective. The page does not note this.
The definition of 'discrétification' and the compatibility conditions across curves (morphisms, the Teichmüller tower) are left implicit.

ideas.what: D-structure on an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0: a compatible choice, for every curve of type (g,ν), of a discrete surface group inside its profinite étale π_1, and the action of field isomorphisms on such structures
ideas.modern_name: no standard name; close to 'discrete/topological structure on profinite Teichmüller tower', comparison étale vs topological π_1 under field automorphisms (conjugate varieties)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Comparison theorem SGA1 (Grothendieck); Galois-conjugate non-homeomorphic varieties: Serre 1964; the systematic 'discretification' viewpoint: not standard
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the discrete vs profinite Teichmüller tower and the Galois action, but not (to my knowledge) this formal notion of D-structure

ideas.what: Special D-structures induced by complex embeddings φ: K̄ → C, and Γ-equivariance of Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄)
ideas.modern_name: equivariance of the comparison isomorphism π_1^top → π̂_1^et under Aut(C)/Galois

ideas.what: Question (developed next page) whether the discrete π_1 data of all curves recover the complex embedding, i.e. injectivity of Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄); equivalently, for K̄ = Q̄, which Galois elements preserve the discrete π_1's
ideas.modern_name: stabilizer in G_Q of the discrete fundamental groups; GT elements of 'discrete type' are {(1,1),(-1,1)}, i.e. identity and complex conjugation

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the notion of a 'D-structure' (compatible discretifications of étale π_1 of all curves) on an arbitrary algebraically closed field K̄ of finite type over Q. He asks how much of the complex embedding is recovered from it; next page: is Hom(K̄,C) → Discspec(K̄) bijective? For K̄ = Q̄ the natural answer seems to be 'injective modulo complex conjugation'. Using ab-ization and the cyclotomic character, σ preserving F_2 ⊂ F̂_2 forces χ(σ) = ±1, then Belyi-type arguments apply. For transcendental K, local constancy in φ suggests non-injectivity, with Hodge structures as the missing invariant. I am not aware of this framework of 'discrete structures on fields' as a characterization of complex embeddings / of G_Q being written up.
missed.quote: D-structure sur K̄ | a) Q̄ ⊂ K̄ b) pour toute courbe alg. X sur K̄ de type g,ν, la donnée d'une discrétification de π_1(X); D structure spéciale par plongement φ : K̄ → C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an anabelian-flavoured characterization of complex embeddings (up to conjugation) by purely group-theoretic 'discrete-in-profinite' data. It is related to the question of which elements of GT or G_Q are 'continuous', and to the interplay of anabelian geometry with Hodge theory, a theme that is only partially explored.

deep.surprise_reason: The equivariance statements are routine, and the Prop as stated is flawed (corrected on the next page). The conceptual move is unusual: axiomatizing 'discrete structures' on fields of finite type via discretifications of profinite π_1 of all curves, and asking whether they recover complex embeddings. It does not seem to appear as such in the literature, but it is a sketch, not a result.
transcription_corrections: 'D structure [-de prima...-] {+spéciale+} par plongement' – reads as 'D structures spéciales: celles définies par plongement φ : K̄ → C' (crossed-out word is likely 'de [première] espèce', unclear).
In the first Prop line, the crossed-out text is 'Soient Θ, Θ' deux'; the main text then begins 'Soient K̄, K̄' deux clôtures algébriques. Pour tout K-isom (plus gén., pour tout isom) K̄ → K̄''.
The second Prop reads 'Soient K̄, K̄' deux clôtures algébriques de K, [munies] de discrét. spéciales Θ, Θ'. Alors il existe un K-isom K̄ → K̄' compatible aux Θ, Θ''.

Cor: 'Deux discrétifications spéciales sur K̄ sont isomorphes par un élt de Γ = Aut_K(K̄)'. The parenthesis seems to read roughly '(ab=, i.e. pas nécessairement par un élément d'un sous-groupe d'indice fini donné de Γ)'; uncertain.
In the NB, the bottom-left factor is Isom(K̄,K̄') with an asterisk footnote mark, not 'Isom_*'. The bottom row is Hom(K̄,C) → Hom(K̄',C).
Last line: likely 'en particulier ... si K̄ = K̄', alors Isom_K(K̄,K̄') = Γ — d'où l'énoncé [la compatibilité]'; final words uncertain.
